subproblems.title: Mass and support of an integer multiplicity current (reuse of the accepted declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (R.Represents T, Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Let μ_R := θ·Hⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) (T.massOn W) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x; and (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and 2.11–2.12 (spt T = spt μ_T), stated in the book without proof. This is the audited proof of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support, whose frozen type is reused verbatim; the parent proof cites it as (MR).
Notation. Hⁿ = μHE[n]; M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For an n-covector α, |α| = |α|_E = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (covectorEuclideanNorm; I runs over strictly increasing multi-indices, e_I = (e_{i₁}, …, e_{iₙ})); dx^I is the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}; ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ := ξ(x)(α).
1. Pointwise algebra. Let x ∈ M be a point where R.orients holds: there are orthonormal τ₁, …, τₙ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. Writing τ_j = Σ_i τ_j^i e_i, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where τ^I is the n×n minor of the matrix (τ_j^i) on the rows I, and the Cauchy–Binet formula gives Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α. The covector ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩·dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), so |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 and ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1. (For n = 0 the only I is empty: |α| = |α()|, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1.) Since R.orients holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, these facts hold μ_R-a.e.; x ↦ ξ^♭(x) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous linear function of ξ (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Integral formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact set tsupport ω ⊆ U, is bounded a.e. by θ·sup|ω| (step 1), and ∫_{M∩tsupport ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R (integration against the density θ).
3. Upper bound. Let W be open and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step 1, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for μ_R-a.e. x, and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W) by step 2. Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
4. Lower bound. Let W be open and t ∈ ℝ with t < μ_R(W); we construct an admissible ω with T(ω) > t, which gives M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Put G := W ∩ U (open); since M ⊆ U, μ_R(G) = μ_R(W). μ_R is a Borel measure finite on compact subsets of U, so on the open σ-compact set G it is a Radon measure, inner regular by compact sets and outer regular on sets of finite measure. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ_R(K) > t + 4η.
 (a) Lusin: there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that ξ^♭|K' is continuous and |ξ^♭| = 1, ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ = 1 μ_R-a.e. on K'.
 (b) There is an open V ⊇ K' with closure(V) compact, closure(V) ⊆ G and μ_R(V ∖ K') < η.
 (c) Extend the coefficients of ξ^♭|K' continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), compose with the radial retraction of the space of n-covectors onto its closed |·|-unit ball, and multiply by a continuous χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V. The resulting continuous g has compact support in V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = ξ^♭ on K'.
 (d) Let g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise convolution with a standard mollifier). For 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V), g_ε is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)| dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_ε → g uniformly as ε → 0; so g_ε is admissible for M_W(T).
 (e) By steps 2 and 1, T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩| dμ_R − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(closure V) ≥ μ_R(K') − η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(closure V) ≥ μ_R(K) − 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(closure V) > t + 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(closure V). As μ_R(closure V) < ∞, T(g_ε) > t for small ε. With step 3 this proves (i).
5. Support. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11) spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Recall x ∈ spt μ_R iff μ_R(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x.
 (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and x ∈ Z, choose such a W with x ∈ W; every admissible form for M_W(T) has T(ω) = 0, so M_W(T) = 0 and μ_R(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. Hence U ∩ spt μ_R ⊆ spt T.
 (b) spt T ⊆ U by definition. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ_R, choose r > 0 with μ_R(B_r(x)) = 0 and closedBall(x, r) ⊆ U (U open). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_r(x), T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = 0 by step 2; so B_r(x) is one of the sets forming Z, x ∈ Z and x ∉ spt T. Hence spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R, which is (ii). ∎
proof_key_steps: For a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|_E (Cauchy–Binet), with equality for the dual covector ξ^♭.
T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R, so admissible forms give T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lusin, Tietze extension, radial retraction and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) arbitrarily close to μ_R(W).
The mass formula identifies the zero region of T with U ∖ spt μ_R.

subproblems.title: Integer multiplicity calculus: tangent locality, restriction, differences, orientation bound (reuse of the accepted declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub)
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) and E ⊆ ℝ^P is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity triple in U and it represents some current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity, then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U ⊆ ℝ^P, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E for every n-covector α (|·|_E the Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M M' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet M' → M ⊆ M' → M' ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M' ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument of Theorem 1.6; Ch. 6, Remarks 2.6, 2.9 and 3.2(1). This is the audited proof of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, whose frozen type is reused verbatim; the parent proof cites these facts as IMC(a)–(d). Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap).
Preliminaries.
(P0) Hⁿ is Borel regular: every set has a Borel hull of the same measure, and SimonGMT's density theorems for the Hausdorff outer measure apply to μHE[n] (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), so null sets and densities transfer verbatim.
(P1) Scaling: Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) for every A (Hausdorff measure scales under dilations and is invariant under isometries). Hence ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y) for Borel A and bounded Borel f.
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, Hⁿ(D ∩ closedBall(x, r)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet: for n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I) over increasing I (A_I the n×n submatrix on the columns I); proved by multilinear expansion of the columns, terms with repeated indices vanishing and the others grouped by permutations.
(P4) Orientation bound: if τ₁, …, τₙ are orthonormal and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α|_E: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I)α(e_I), and by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3) |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E·det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|_E, AAᵀ being the identity. (For n = 0, |α()| = |α|_E.)
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace differ by a sign: orthonormal bases τ, τ' of Q satisfy τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ). Also −ζ is a unit orientation of Q whenever ζ is.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).
1. Part (d). By the orientation field of R, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α|_E. (No openness of U is needed.)
2. Part (a). Let D := M' ∖ M. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P): open, closure(U_R) compact ⊆ U, U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R has Hⁿ(D_R ∩ closedBall(x, r)) = o(rⁿ). Let Z' ⊇ ⋃_R Z_R be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). For x ∈ M ∖ Z' choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with closedBall(x, r₀) ⊆ U_R; then x ∉ D_R and D ∩ closedBall(x, r) = D_R ∩ closedBall(x, r) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ closedBall(x, r)) = o(rⁿ). For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0) and r < r₀/ρ, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D) (η injective), and by (P1) |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f|·r^{−n}Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0. So for every f both families of integrals have the same limits as r ↓ 0, and the dimension condition finrank Q = n is common: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for all x ∈ M ∖ Z' and all Q.
3. Part (b). Let R' have carrier M ∩ E, mult θ and orient ξ. Its fields hold: M ∩ E is Borel and ⊆ U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ measurable and positive on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K}θ ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M. Orientation: by (P6) and part (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E, M ∩ E and M have the same approximate tangent spaces at x; with the orientation field of R this gives that of R'. The current A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U)) is well defined and linear (integrand bounded by sup|ω|_E·θ·1_{tsupport ω} a.e. by (d)); if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (supports in a fixed compact C ⊆ U, uniform convergence; all norms on n-covectors are equivalent) then |A(ω_j)| ≤ sup|ω_j|_E·∫_{M∩C}θ → 0. So A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and R' represents A.
4. Part (c). Let R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A), R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B) represent A, B.
 (i) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B. Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and M_A has an approximate tangent space Q_A(x) at x oriented by ξ_A(x); likewise for B; and for each pair (N, N') ∈ {(M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B)} with x ∈ N, N and N' have the same approximate tangent spaces at x. By the orientation fields, (P6) and part (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing it.
 (ii) For x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀ the approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x equals Q_A(x) and Q_B(x) (uniqueness, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {±1} (ε Borel).
 (iii) With O := (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀ and k := θ_A − εθ_B ∈ ℤ on O, put M := ((M_A ∖ M_B) ∪ (M_B ∖ M_A) ∪ {x ∈ O : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀, θ := θ_A on M_A ∖ M_B, θ_B on M_B ∖ M_A, |k| on O, 0 elsewhere, and ζ := ξ̃_A on M_A ∖ M_B, −ξ̃_B on M_B ∖ M_A, sign(k)ξ̃_A on O, 0 elsewhere. For every x ∉ N₀: θ(x)1_M(x)ζ(x) = θ_A(x)1_{M_A}(x)ξ̃_A(x) − θ_B(x)1_{M_B}(x)ξ̃_B(x).
 (iv) Integrating ⟨ω, ·⟩ (all integrands integrable by (d), θ1_M ≤ θ_A1_{M_A} + θ_B1_{M_B}): ∫_M θ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) − B(ω) = (A − B)(ω).
 (v) M is Borel, ⊆ U, countably n-rectifiable (subset of M_A ∪ M_B); θ is Borel, ℕ-valued, ≥ 1 on M, locally integrable; ζ is Borel. Orientation: Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U by (P6); part (a) for M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A, M ∩ M_A ⊆ M, M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B, M ∩ M_B ⊆ M shows that a.e. on M ∩ M_A (resp. M ∩ M_B) the approximate tangent spaces of M and M_A (resp. M_B) agree, and ζ(x) = ±ξ_A(x) (resp. −ξ_B(x)) is a unit orientation of it by (P5).
 So (M, θ, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A − B. ∎
proof_key_steps: (P1)–(P2): blow-ups scale Hⁿ by r^{−n}, and a Borel set of finite measure has density zero at a.e. point of its complement.
(a) Density zero of M′ ∖ M makes the blow-up integrals of M and M′ asymptotically equal, so the tangent spaces agree a.e. on M.
(b) Restriction keeps all IMRep fields (tangent spaces by (a)) and the restricted integral is a continuous current.
(c) On the overlap the orientations differ by a sign; the combined multiplicity θ_A − εθ_B, restricted to where it is nonzero, gives an IMRep of A − B.
(d) Cauchy–Binet and Cauchy–Schwarz give |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|_E for unit simple ξ.

subproblems.title: Vectors of an approximate tangent plane are attained by blow-ups of the set (reuse of the accepted declaration dsmc_att_blowUp_points_of_approxTangent)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and M, N ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Let x ∈ ℝ^P and let Q be a linear subspace such that M has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} g dHⁿ → ∫_Q g dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x)). Let w ∈ Q and s > 0. Then there is λ₀ > 0 such that for every λ ∈ (0, λ₀) some y ∈ M ∩ N satisfies |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| < s.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M N : Set (Euclid P)) (x w : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), μHE[n] (M \ N) = 0 → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → w ∈ Q → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∃ lam₀ : ℝ, 0 < lam₀ ∧ ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → lam < lam₀ → ∃ y ∈ M ∩ N, ‖lam⁻¹ • (y - x) - w‖ < s
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the secant argument in step 7 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4): a positive test function concentrated near a point of Q has positive integral over Q, so the blow-ups of M must charge every neighbourhood of that point. This is the audited proof of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dsmc_att_blowUp_points_of_approxTangent, whose frozen type is reused verbatim, with the two auxiliary facts proved inline.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η_λ(y) := λ⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x λ). For S ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_S g dHⁿ := ∫ g d(Hⁿ⌞S), where (Hⁿ⌞S)(B) = Hⁿ(B ∩ S) for Borel B (S need not be measurable).
1. Test function. g(y) := max(0, s − |y − w|) is continuous, g ≥ 0, g(w) = s > 0, and g(y) = 0 whenever |y − w| ≥ s; so g has compact support (in closedBall(w, s)) and {g ≠ 0} ⊆ ball(w, s). Regard g as an element of C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
2. Positivity on the plane. Since dim Q = n there is a linear isometry ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P onto Q. μHE[n] is invariant under isometries (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ, so Hⁿ⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure under ι and ∫_Q g dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} g(ι(u)) du. The integrand is continuous, ≥ 0, and > s/2 on the ball of radius s/2 about u₀ := ι⁻¹(w), which has positive Lebesgue measure. Hence I := ∫_Q g dHⁿ > 0.
3. Choice of λ₀. By the convergence clause of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q applied to g, F(λ) := ∫_{η_λ(M)} g dHⁿ → I as λ ↓ 0. Since I > 0, there is λ₀ > 0 with F(λ) > 0 for every λ ∈ (0, λ₀). Fix λ ∈ (0, λ₀) and put S := η_λ(M).
4. The blow-up charges the ball. If Hⁿ(S ∩ ball(w, s)) = 0, then, the ball being Borel, (Hⁿ⌞S)(ball(w, s)) = 0; as {g ≠ 0} ⊆ ball(w, s), g = 0 Hⁿ⌞S-a.e. and F(λ) = 0, a contradiction. So Hⁿ(S ∩ ball(w, s)) > 0.
5. The exceptional part is null. η_λ is λ⁻¹-Lipschitz, so Hⁿ(η_λ(M ∖ N)) ≤ λ^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 (Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, the normalizing factor of μHE[n] being a constant).
6. Covering. If z ∈ S ∩ ball(w, s), then z = η_λ(y) with y ∈ M; either y ∈ N, so z ∈ η_λ(M ∩ N) ∩ ball(w, s), or y ∈ M ∖ N and z ∈ η_λ(M ∖ N). Hence S ∩ ball(w, s) ⊆ (η_λ(M ∩ N) ∩ ball(w, s)) ∪ η_λ(M ∖ N).
7. By steps 4–6, monotonicity and subadditivity of the outer measure Hⁿ, Hⁿ(η_λ(M ∩ N) ∩ ball(w, s)) > 0; in particular this set is nonempty. Take z in it: z = η_λ(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x) for some y ∈ M ∩ N and |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| = |z − w| < s. As λ ∈ (0, λ₀) was arbitrary, λ₀ has the required property. ∎
proof_key_steps: The tent function g = max(0, s − |· − w|) is in C_c, vanishes off ball(w, s) and has ∫_Q g dHⁿ > 0 (Hⁿ⌞Q is Lebesgue measure on Q).
Approximate-tangent convergence gives ∫_{η_λ(M)} g dHⁿ > 0 for all λ ∈ (0, λ₀), so Hⁿ(η_λ(M) ∩ ball(w, s)) > 0.
η_λ is Lipschitz, so η_λ(M ∖ N) is Hⁿ-null; hence η_λ(M ∩ N) meets ball(w, s), giving y ∈ M ∩ N with |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| < s.

subproblems.title: Unit orientations under linear maps: |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ, and invariance when L fixes the oriented plane
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Q ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace, ξ an n-vector (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) that is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) with span τ = Q and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} such that ξ(β) = s·β(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every n-covector β), and L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a continuous linear map. For an n-covector α let α∘L be the n-covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ) (α.compContinuousLinearMap L). Then (a) |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ for every n-covector α, where |·|_E is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm) and ‖L‖ the operator norm; and (b) if Lv = v for every v ∈ Q, then ξ(α∘L) = ξ(α) for every n-covector α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ (α.compContinuousLinearMap L)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α * ‖L‖ ^ n) ∧ ((∀ v ∈ Q, L v = v) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ (α.compContinuousLinearMap L) = ξ α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the algebra items (L0)–(L2) of the parent proof (used in its steps 4 and 11) and the computation ξ(x)(β∘ΛⁿDf(x)) = ±β(Df(x)τ) = ±β(τ) = ξ(x)(β) at the end of its step 7. Notation: e = (e₁, …, e_P) the standard basis of ℝ^P; |β|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm β = (Σ_{I increasing} β(e_I)²)^{1/2} for a k-covector β, e_I := (e_{i₁}, …, e_{i_k}); ‖L‖ the operator norm; α∘L := α.compContinuousLinearMap L.
1. (L0) For a k-covector β and any orthonormal basis b = (b₁, …, b_P) of ℝ^P, S_b(β) := Σ_{i₁,…,i_k ∈ {1..P}} β(b_{i₁}, …, b_{i_k})² equals k!·|β|²_E. Proof. (i) S_b does not depend on b: for any k-linear γ and fixed w₂, …, w_k, Σ_i γ(b_i, w₂, …, w_k)² = |g|², where g is the vector representing the linear form γ(·, w₂, …, w_k) (Parseval for the orthonormal basis b); so the first slot's basis can be replaced by e without changing the sum, and likewise every other slot, one at a time; hence S_b(β) = S_e(β). (ii) For b = e: tuples with a repeated index contribute 0 (β alternating); a tuple with distinct entries is I∘σ for a unique increasing I and a unique permutation σ, and β(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)β(e_I); each I occurs k! times. Hence S_e(β) = k!·Σ_I β(e_I)² = k!|β|²_E.
2. (L1) For an n-covector α and a linear L: |α∘L|_E ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ|α|_E. Proof. For an n-linear γ put ‖γ‖²_HS := Σ_{i₁,…,iₙ} γ(e_{i₁}, …, e_{iₙ})². Let γ' be γ with its first slot precomposed with L. For fixed later arguments let g represent γ(·, w₂, …, wₙ); then Σ_i γ(Le_i, w₂, …)² = Σ_i ⟨g, Le_i⟩² = Σ_i ⟨Lᵀg, e_i⟩² = |Lᵀg|² ≤ ‖L‖²|g|² = ‖L‖²·Σ_i γ(e_i, w₂, …)². Summing over the remaining indices gives ‖γ'‖²_HS ≤ ‖L‖²‖γ‖²_HS. Precomposing the n slots one after the other, ‖α∘L‖²_HS ≤ ‖L‖^{2n}‖α‖²_HS. By step 1 (b = e, k = n) both sides equal n! times the squared Euclidean norms, so |α∘L|_E ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ|α|_E.
3. (L2) For an n-covector β and an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ: |β(τ)| ≤ |β|_E. Proof. Extend τ to an orthonormal basis b of ℝ^P with b_j = τ_j for j ≤ n. In S_b(β) = n!|β|²_E (step 1) keep only the n! tuples that are permutations σ of (1, …, n): each contributes β(τ_{σ(1)}, …, τ_{σ(n)})² = β(τ)², and the omitted terms are ≥ 0. Hence n!·β(τ)² ≤ n!|β|²_E. (For n = 0, β(τ) = β() and |β|_E = |β()|.)
4. Set-up. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q choose τ orthonormal with span τ = Q and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(β) = s·β(τ) for every n-covector β.
5. Part (a). For an n-covector α, ξ(α∘L) = s·(α∘L)(τ). By step 3 applied to β := α∘L and then step 2: |ξ(α∘L)| = |(α∘L)(τ)| ≤ |α∘L|_E ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ|α|_E = |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ.
6. Part (b). Assume Lv = v for every v ∈ Q. Each τ_i lies in span τ = Q, so Lτ_i = τ_i, hence (α∘L)(τ) = α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ) = α(τ) and ξ(α∘L) = s·α(τ) = ξ(α) for every α. ∎
proof_key_steps: (L0) Σ over all index tuples of β(b_{i₁},…,b_{i_k})² equals k!|β|²_E for every orthonormal basis b (Parseval slot by slot).
(L1) Precomposing one slot with L multiplies the Hilbert–Schmidt norm by at most ‖L‖, so |α∘L|_E ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ|α|_E.
(L2) Extending τ to an orthonormal basis, β(τ)² is dominated by |β|²_E.
(a) |ξ(α∘L)| = |(α∘L)(τ)| ≤ |α∘L|_E ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ|α|_E; (b) L fixes τ, so (α∘L)(τ) = α(τ).

subproblems.title: Carrier, mass and support facts for integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and write 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) for GeometricCurrentOn univ n. (1) Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be represented by an integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n, R.Represents Y), and let μ_R := θ·Hⁿ⌞M (R.measure, Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0, the total mass satisfies M(Y) = μ_R(ℝ^P) (Y.mass = R.measure univ), and if spt Y is compact then μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞. (2) For all Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P): spt Y₁ is closed, and spt(Y₁ − Y₂) ⊆ spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂, where Y₁ − Y₂ is the pointwise difference of currents.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), R.Represents Y → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ Y.support) = 0 ∧ Y.mass = R.measure univ ∧ (IsCompact Y.support → R.measure univ ≠ ∞)) ∧ ∀ Y₁ Y₂ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsClosed Y₁.support ∧ (Y₁ - Y₂).support ⊆ Y₁.support ∪ Y₂.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (finite mass; Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0) and step 6 (support of a difference; supports in ℝ^P are closed) of the parent proof. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]; in (1), M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, K := spt Y. All currents have the open domain U = ℝ^P.
1. By the sibling mass_and_support with U = ℝ^P (open) and T = Y: (i) M_W(Y) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and (ii) spt Y = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_R = spt μ_R.
2. Mass. The total mass of a current with domain ℝ^P is its local mass on the domain: M(Y) = M_{ℝ^P}(Y) (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.mass = massOn of the domain). By 1(i) with W = ℝ^P, M(Y) = μ_R(ℝ^P).
3. Null complement of the support. ℝ^P is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so the complement of the support of any measure ν on ℝ^P is ν-null: it is the union of the open ν-null sets, and countably many of them already cover it (Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support). With 1(ii), μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0.
4. K is closed (step 6 below), so ℝ^P ∖ K is Borel and μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = ∫_{M∖K} θ dHⁿ (definition of the density measure μ_R on a Borel set). Since θ ≥ 1 on M (R.mult_pos, θ integer-valued), Hⁿ(M ∖ K) ≤ ∫_{M∖K} θ dHⁿ = 0. Hence Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0.
5. Finiteness. If K is compact, then by step 3, μ_R(ℝ^P) = μ_R(K) + μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ, which is finite by R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set K ⊆ ℝ^P.
6. Closedness. For Y₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), spt Y₁ = ℝ^P ∖ Z(Y₁), where the zero region Z(Y₁) is the union of the open sets W with compact closure on which Y₁ vanishes (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support and zeroRegion); a union of open sets is open, so spt Y₁ is closed.
7. Support of a difference. Let x ∉ spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂. As x ∈ ℝ^P, x ∈ Z(Y₁) ∩ Z(Y₂): there are open sets W₁, W₂ containing x, with compact closures (contained in ℝ^P), such that Y_i(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W_i (i = 1, 2). Then W := W₁ ∩ W₂ is open, contains x, and closure(W) ⊆ closure(W₁) is compact (a closed subset of a compact set). For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W we have tsupport ω ⊆ W₁ and ⊆ W₂, so (Y₁ − Y₂)(ω) = Y₁(ω) − Y₂(ω) = 0 (the difference of currents is evaluated pointwise). Thus W is one of the sets forming Z(Y₁ − Y₂), x ∈ Z(Y₁ − Y₂) and x ∉ spt(Y₁ − Y₂). ∎
proof_key_steps: mass_and_support (U = ℝ^P) gives M_W(Y) = μ_R(W) for open W and spt Y = spt μ_R; with W = ℝ^P, M(Y) = μ_R(ℝ^P).
μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ spt μ_R) = 0 (second countability), and θ ≥ 1 on M gives Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0.
For compact spt Y, μ_R(ℝ^P) = ∫_{M∩spt Y} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by local integrability of θ.
Supports are complements of open zero regions; a common relatively compact neighbourhood where Y₁ and Y₂ vanish lies in the zero region of Y₁ − Y₂.

subproblems.title: The push-forward formula defines a current with compact support in f(K) (Simon 6.2.23–2.24(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), K ⊆ U compact with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), O ⊆ ℝ^P open with K ⊆ O, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O) with f(K) ⊆ U. Then there is Q ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) with Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x and (β∘A)(v₁, …, vₙ) = β(Av₁, …, Avₙ) (β.compContinuousLinearMap A); moreover spt Q is compact and spt Q ⊆ f(K).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K O : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ K) = 0 → IsOpen O → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → f '' K ⊆ U → ∃ Q : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Q ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∂μHE[n]) ∧ IsCompact Q.support ∧ Q.support ⊆ f '' K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24(2)): the parent's push Y is defined by this integral, shown to be a current by the bound |push Y(ω)| ≤ const·|ω|_∞, and to have support in f(spt Y). Here the representation R is fixed, spt Y is replaced by the compact set K carrying Hⁿ⌞M, and the domain ℝ^P by an open U.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; ‖·‖ denotes operator norms (of linear maps, of n-covectors as continuous alternating maps, of n-vectors). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) put β_ω(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) and ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_z ‖ω(z)‖ < ∞ (ω continuous with compact support).
1. Good points. By R.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) and s ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ) for every n-covector β; at such x, |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖·Π_i|τ_i| = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). Since Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M is such a point lying in K. Put c_K := ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult; K is compact and K ⊆ U).
2. Derivative bound. f is C¹ on the open set O, so f and Df are continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn, ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen); K ⊆ O is compact, so Λ_K := sup_{x∈K}‖Df(x)‖ < ∞ (Λ_K := 0 if K = ∅).
3. The integrand. For every n-covector α and linear A, ‖α∘A‖ ≤ ‖α‖·‖A‖ⁿ (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le); so ‖β_ω(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω‖_∞Λ_Kⁿ for x ∈ K. On O, x ↦ β_ω(x) is continuous (ω, f, Df continuous and (α, A) ↦ α∘A continuous), so x ↦ 1_K(x)β_ω(x) is Borel. Because Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, the integrand x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(β_ω(x)) agrees Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. with θ(x)ξ(x)(1_K(x)β_ω(x)), which is a.e. strongly measurable (θ Borel, ξ a.e. strongly measurable, evaluation continuous) and, by steps 1–2, bounded a.e. by ‖ω‖_∞Λ_Kⁿθ(x)1_K(x). Hence it is integrable and I(ω) := ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(β_ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) satisfies |I(ω)| ≤ Λ_Kⁿ·c_K·‖ω‖_∞. (This is the parent's remark in step 3 that the Bochner integral is no junk value, and its bound of step 4.)
4. Linearity. β_{aω+bη} = a·β_ω + b·β_η (evaluation at f(x) and α ↦ α∘Df(x) are linear) and ξ(x) is linear; all integrands are integrable (step 3), so I(aω + bη) = a·I(ω) + b·I(η). Thus I is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U).
5. Continuity (parent step 4). Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0): there is a compact C ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ C for all j, and the k = 0 clause says ω_j → 0 uniformly on C (iteratedFDeriv of order 0 is ω_j composed with a norm-preserving identification). Since ω_j = 0 off C, ‖ω_j‖_∞ → 0, and by step 3 |I(ω_j)| ≤ Λ_Kⁿc_K‖ω_j‖_∞ → 0. Hence Q := I is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with the required formula.
6. Vanishing away from f(K) (parent step 5). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅. For x ∈ K, f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(f(x)) = 0 and β_ω(x) = 0; the integrand vanishes on M ∩ K, hence Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., and Q(ω) = 0.
7. Support. f is continuous on K, so f(K) is compact, hence closed, and f(K) ⊆ U. Let z ∈ U ∖ f(K). As U ∖ f(K) is open, there is r > 0 with closedBall(z, r) ⊆ U ∖ f(K). W := ball(z, r) is open, closure(W) = closedBall(z, r) is compact and contained in U, and Q vanishes on W: if tsupport ω ⊆ W then tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅ and Q(ω) = 0 by step 6. So W lies in the zero region of Q, z ∉ spt Q; as spt Q ⊆ U by definition, spt Q ⊆ f(K).
8. Compactness. spt Q = U ∖ Z(Q) with Z(Q) the (open) zero region; by step 7 and f(K) ⊆ U, spt Q = f(K) ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ Z(Q)), a closed subset of the compact set f(K), hence compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: A.e. on M, ξ(x) is a unit simple n-vector, so |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖, and a.e. x ∈ M lies in K.

Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the extension Ȳ of Y to forms continuous near spt Y, obtained as lim_σ Y(γ_σ) for mollifications γ_σ of χγ), specialized to γ := f^#ω. The point is that the approximating test forms depend only on (f, ω, O, K), so the limit is the same for every Y and every representation R, which yields representation independence and additivity in the parent.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; ‖·‖ the operator norm of n-covectors; γ(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) for x ∈ ℝ^P.
1. Continuity of γ on O. f is C¹ on the open set O, so f and Df are continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn, ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen); ω is continuous; and (β, A) ↦ β∘A is continuous on (n-covectors) × (linear maps) (finite-dimensional, polynomial in the entries; ‖β∘A − β'∘A'‖ ≤ ‖β − β'‖‖A‖ⁿ + ‖β'‖·n·max(‖A‖, ‖A'‖)^{n−1}‖A − A'‖). Hence γ is continuous on O.
2. Cutoff. K is compact and O is open, so (smooth Urysohn lemma; e.g. a finite sum of ContDiffBump functions, or Mathlib exists_contMDiff_zero_iff_one_iff_of_isClosed) there is χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, compact tsupport χ ⊆ O and χ = 1 on an open set W₀ ⊇ K. Define h(x) := χ(x)γ(x) for x ∈ O and h(x) := 0 for x ∉ O. Then h is continuous on ℝ^P (on the open set O as a product of continuous maps; on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport χ it vanishes identically; these two open sets cover ℝ^P because tsupport χ ⊆ O), h has compact support contained in tsupport χ, and h = γ on W₀ ⊇ K. Put B := sup_x ‖h(x)‖ < ∞.
3. Test forms. Let ρ_j ≥ 0 be smooth mollifiers with ∫ρ_j = 1 and support in ball(0, 1/(j+1)), and ω_j := h ∗ ρ_j (convolution in the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors). Each ω_j is C^∞ (convolution with a smooth compactly supported kernel) with compact support (in the 1-neighbourhood of tsupport h), so ω_j ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (the support condition tsupport ω_j ⊆ ℝ^P is trivial). Since h is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support), δ_j := sup_x ‖ω_j(x) − h(x)‖ → 0, and ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ B. The sequence (ω_j) depends only on f, ω, O and K (through χ), not on Y or R.
4. Fix Y and R = (M, θ, ξ) with R.Represents Y and spt Y ⊆ K. By the sibling carrier_facts (part (1)), Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0, hence Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. By R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set K, c := ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. By R.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal τ and s ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ), so |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for every n-covector β (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm, Π|τ_i| = 1).
5. Rewriting both sides. Since R represents Y, Y(ω_j) = R.action ω_j = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω_j(x)) dHⁿ(x). Since h = γ on K and Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, the functions x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(γ(x)) and x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(h(x)) agree Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., so their integrals over M coincide (integral_congr_ae; in particular the left integrand is a.e. strongly measurable). The functions θξ(ω_j) and θξ(h) are a.e. strongly measurable (ω_j, h continuous; θ Borel; ξ a.e. strongly measurable) and bounded a.e. by B·θ·1_K (step 4, Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0), hence integrable.

proof_key_steps: γ = f^#ω is continuous on O; a smooth cutoff χ (χ = 1 near K, tsupport χ ⊆ O) makes h = χγ a continuous compactly supported form equal to γ near K.
Mollifications ω_j = h ∗ ρ_j are test forms converging uniformly to h; they depend only on f, ω, O, K.
For any R representing Y with spt Y ⊆ K: Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (carrier_facts), ∫_{M∩K}θ < ∞, and |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ a.e.
Y(ω_j) = ∫_M θξ(ω_j) and ∫_M θξ(γ) = ∫_M θξ(h); the difference is ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ·sup‖ω_j − h‖ → 0.

subproblems.title: Mass bound M(Z) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y) for a current Z given by the push-forward formula

Let Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) representing Y, with spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ O. Suppose Z(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)). Then M(Z) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Lⁿ)·M(Y) for the total masses (Z.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ n) * Y.mass).

Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("For |ω| ≤ 1, push Y(ω) ≤ LⁿY.mass, so ENNReal.ofReal(push Y(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(L^{m+1})·Y.mass; take the supremum", using (L1)–(L2) at good points), applied to any current Z given by the formula; the empty-domain case is the parent's remark "L ≥ 0 if O ≠ ∅; if O = ∅, K = ∅".
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; |·|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm; μ_R := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M; K := spt Y.
1. By the sibling carrier_facts (part (1)): Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, M(Y) = μ_R(ℝ^P), and μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞ (K compact). Hence θ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable and ∫_M θ dHⁿ = μ_R(ℝ^P).toReal (θ ≥ 0, μ_R(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_M θ dHⁿ < ∞).
2. Case L < 0. Then O = ∅ (for y ∈ O, 0 ≤ ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L would be impossible), so K = ∅ and Hⁿ(M) = Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0; every integral over M vanishes, Z(ω) = 0 for all ω, and M(Z) = sup ENNReal.ofReal(0) = 0 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Lⁿ)·M(Y). Assume from now on L ≥ 0.
3. Pointwise bound. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) be admissible for M(Z) = M_{ℝ^P}(Z) (Z.massOn univ): |ω(z)|_E ≤ 1 for every z. For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x: x ∈ K ⊆ O (step 1), and by R.orients ξ(x) is a unit orientation of some subspace (IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x). At such x the sibling orient_comp, part (a), with L := Df(x) and α := ω(f(x)) gives |ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x))| ≤ |ω(f(x))|_E·‖Df(x)‖ⁿ ≤ 1·Lⁿ, since 0 ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ L. Hence |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x))| ≤ Lⁿθ(x) for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x.
4. Integral bound. The bound ‖∫F‖ ≤ ∫G holds whenever ‖F‖ ≤ G a.e. with G integrable, whether or not F is integrable (Bochner convention ∫F = 0 for non-integrable F; Mathlib norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). With G := Lⁿθ and steps 1, 3: |Z(ω)| ≤ Lⁿ∫_M θ dHⁿ = Lⁿ·μ_R(ℝ^P).toReal.

Hence ENNReal.ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Lⁿ·μ_R(ℝ^P).toReal) = ENNReal.ofReal(Lⁿ)·ENNReal.ofReal(μ_R(ℝ^P).toReal) = ENNReal.ofReal(Lⁿ)·μ_R(ℝ^P) = ENNReal.ofReal(Lⁿ)·M(Y) (Lⁿ ≥ 0, μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞). For admissible ω (|ω|_E ≤ 1) and a.e. x ∈ M ⊆ spt Y ⊆ O: orient_comp (a) gives |ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x))| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ⁿ ≤ Lⁿ.

subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Let Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) representing Y, with spt Y ⊆ O and f(y) = y for every y ∈ spt Y. Suppose Z(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (Hⁿ = μHE[n], Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x, ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)). Then Z = Y.

Source: step 7 of the parent proof. The parent's secant claim (every vector of the approximate tangent plane is a limit of secant directions of points of the set near x) is used in the blow-up form supplied by the sibling blowup_points, applied to M and N := spt Y; this replaces the parent's use of IMC(a) for M ∩ K.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; K := spt Y; Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x.
1. By the sibling carrier_facts (part (1)), Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0.
2. Good points. For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x: x ∈ K (step 1), and (R.orients) there is a linear subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Fix such an x and Q.
3. Differentiability. x ∈ K ⊆ O with O open and f C¹ on O, so f is differentiable at x with derivative Df(x); and f(x) = x since x ∈ K.
4. Claim: Df(x)w = w for every w ∈ Q. Fix w ∈ Q. For each k ≥ 1 apply blowup_points to (M, N := K, x, w, Q) with s := 1/k (its hypotheses: Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 by step 1 and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q): there is λ₀(k) > 0 such that every λ ∈ (0, λ₀(k)) admits y ∈ M ∩ K with |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| < 1/k. Choose λ_k ∈ (0, min(λ₀(k), 1/k)) and such y_k, and put u_k := λ_k⁻¹(y_k − x). Then |u_k − w| < 1/k, so u_k → w and |u_k| ≤ |w| + 1, and y_k − x = λ_k u_k → 0. Since y_k ∈ K, f(y_k) = y_k; also f(x) = x. By differentiability at x, f(y_k) − f(x) − Df(x)(y_k − x) = r_k with |r_k| ≤ ε_k|y_k − x| and ε_k → 0 (ε_k := 0 if y_k = x). Hence λ_k u_k − Df(x)(λ_k u_k) = r_k, and dividing by λ_k > 0: |u_k − Df(x)u_k| ≤ ε_k|u_k| ≤ ε_k(|w| + 1) → 0. Letting k → ∞ (Df(x) is continuous): w − Df(x)w = 0.
5. Orientation invariance. By step 4, Df(x)v = v for all v ∈ Q; the sibling orient_comp, part (b), with L := Df(x) gives ξ(x)(α∘Df(x)) = ξ(x)(α) for every n-covector α. With α := ω(f(x)) = ω(x) (f(x) = x): θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) = θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)).
6. Conclusion. For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) the integrands of Z(ω) and of R.action ω agree Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (steps 2–5), so Z(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) = R.action ω = Y(ω) (R represents Y). Currents agreeing on every test form are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so Z = Y. ∎

blowup_points (with N = spt Y) yields y_k ∈ M ∩ spt Y and λ_k → 0 with λ_k⁻¹(y_k − x) → w for each w ∈ Q.
f(y_k) = y_k, f(x) = x and differentiability at x give Df(x)w = w on Q.
orient_comp (b) gives ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) = ξ(x)(ω(x)) a.e., so Z(ω) = R.action ω = Y(ω) and Z = Y by extensionality.

subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), K ⊆ U compact with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), O ⊆ ℝ^P open with K ⊆ O, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O. Let Q ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x, ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)). If ∂X = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes X; vacuous for n = 0), then ∂Q = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes Q).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(1): ∂f_#T = f_#∂T), with spt Y replaced by the compact set K carrying Hⁿ⌞M, ℝ^P by an open domain U, and the parent's appeal to (VO) replaced by the representation (a test form vanishing on K is killed by X because Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0).
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; ‖·‖ operator norms. For a C^∞ map h : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and a p-form α, h^#α(x) := α(h(x))∘Dh(x) = (α (h x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ h x).
0. Reduction. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes Q holds by definition. Let n = m + 1. BoundaryVanishes Q means Q.boundary = 0, i.e. Q(dβ) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U), where dβ := exteriorDerivative β ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (Simon 6.2.3; SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); likewise the hypothesis gives X(dβ') = 0 for every β' ∈ 𝒟^m(U). If K = ∅ then Hⁿ(M) = 0, every integral over M vanishes, Q = 0 and ∂Q = 0; so assume K ≠ ∅.
1. Local facts. By R.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ, hence |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every n-covector α. c := ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Consequently (*): if γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) vanishes on K, then X(γ) = R.action γ = ∫_M θξ(γ) dHⁿ = 0, since the integrand vanishes on M ∩ K and Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0.
2. Cutoffs. K is compact and O ∩ U is an open set containing K, so there is δ > 0 with K' := {z : dist(z, K) ≤ 2δ} ⊆ O ∩ U; K' is compact. By the smooth Urysohn lemma choose χ₁ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ χ₁ ≤ 1, with compact tsupport χ₁ ⊆ O and χ₁ = 1 on K', and put g := χ₁·f on O, g := 0 off O. Then g is C¹ on ℝ^P (C¹ on the open set O; identically 0 on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport χ₁; these cover ℝ^P) with compact support, and g = f on K', so g(x) = f(x) and Dg(x) = Df(x) for every x in the interior of K', which contains K. Choose also ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, with ζ = 1 on an open set W ⊇ K and tsupport ζ ⊆ {z : dist(z, K) ≤ δ}, a compact subset of U.
3. Mollification. Let ρ_σ (σ > 0) be standard mollifiers and g_σ := g ∗ ρ_σ (componentwise). g_σ is C^∞, Dg_σ = (Dg) ∗ ρ_σ, and since g and Dg are uniformly continuous with compact support, g_σ → g and Dg_σ → Dg uniformly on ℝ^P as σ ↓ 0; moreover ‖Dg_σ(x)‖ ≤ C := sup_z‖Dg(z)‖ for all σ and x.
4. Approximating functionals. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ζ·g_σ^#ω is C^∞ (compositions and products of C^∞ maps; (α, A) ↦ α∘A is polynomial) with tsupport contained in tsupport ζ, a compact subset of U; so ζ·g_σ^#ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Put X_σ(ω) := X(ζ·g_σ^#ω). Similarly ζ·g_σ^#β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) for β ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
5. (a) X_σ(ω) → Q(ω) as σ ↓ 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Since R represents X, X_σ(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ζ(x)g_σ^#ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(g_σ^#ω(x)) dHⁿ(x), because Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M lies in K, where ζ = 1. For x ∈ K, g_σ^#ω(x) = ω(g_σ(x))∘Dg_σ(x) → ω(g(x))∘Dg(x) = ω(f(x))∘Df(x) uniformly in x ∈ K: ω is bounded and uniformly continuous, g_σ → g and Dg_σ → Dg uniformly with ‖Dg_σ‖ ≤ C, and ‖α∘A − α'∘A'‖ ≤ ‖α − α'‖‖A‖ⁿ + ‖α'‖·n·max(‖A‖, ‖A'‖)^{n−1}‖A − A'‖. Hence, by step 1, |X_σ(ω) − Q(ω)| ≤ c·sup_{x∈K}‖g_σ^#ω(x) − ω(f(x))∘Df(x)‖ → 0 (both integrands are integrable: a.e. strongly measurable on M ∩ K and bounded there by θ·sup‖ω‖·max(C, sup_K‖Df‖)ⁿ).
 (b) X_σ(dβ) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Since g_σ is C^∞ on ℝ^P, SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin (with U = V = ℝ^P, where fderivWithin over ℝ^P is fderiv; Simon 6.1.14) gives d(g_σ^#β) = g_σ^#(dβ) on ℝ^P. Hence X_σ(dβ) = X(ζ·d(g_σ^#β)). On the open set W, ζ·g_σ^#β = g_σ^#β, so d(ζ·g_σ^#β) = d(g_σ^#β) = ζ·d(g_σ^#β) on W (the exterior derivative at a point depends only on the germ of the form there). Therefore γ := ζ·d(g_σ^#β) − d(ζ·g_σ^#β) is a test form in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (both terms are) that vanishes on W ⊇ K, and X(γ) = 0 by (*). So X_σ(dβ) = X(d(ζ·g_σ^#β)) = (∂X)(ζ·g_σ^#β) = 0.
6. Conclusion. For β ∈ 𝒟^m(U), dβ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); by 5(a) and 5(b), Q(dβ) = lim_{σ↓0} X_σ(dβ) = 0. Hence Q.boundary = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes Q. ∎

subproblems.title: The push-forward of an integer multiplicity current by a C¹ map is integer multiplicity (Simon 6.3.3–3.9)
subproblems.statement: Assume (TL): for all P', n' ∈ ℕ, every open U' ⊆ ℝ^{P'} and all Borel sets A ⊆ B ⊆ U' with Hⁿ'(B ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U', for Hⁿ'-a.e. x ∈ A and every linear subspace Q, B has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' B x Q) if and only if A does. Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), K ⊆ U compact with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), O ⊆ ℝ^P open with K ⊆ O, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O with f(K) ⊆ U, and Q ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x, ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)). Then Q is integer multiplicity: Q = τ(N', θ', ξ') for some integer multiplicity triple in U (IsIntegerMultiplicity Q).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 9–11 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9; the integrality sketch 3.5–3.8 replaced by a bi-Lipschitz parametrization, tangent planes along the pieces and the area formula), generalized from the domain ℝ^P and K = spt Y to an open U and a compact K carrying Hⁿ⌞M. The parent's IMC(a) is the hypothesis (TL) here. As in the parent, the carrier is finally restricted to the points of nonzero multiplicity (oppositely oriented sheets with the same image cancel).
Notation and algebra. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; on ℝⁿ (Euclid n) it is Lebesgue measure Lⁿ. |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I increasing} α(e_I)²)^{1/2} for a k-covector α (e the standard basis of ℝ^P). For a linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P let A_#e be the n-vector α ↦ α(Ae₁, …, Aeₙ) (e₁, …, eₙ the standard basis of ℝⁿ) and J_A := det(⟨Ae_i, Ae_j⟩)^{1/2} ≥ 0 (the area Jacobian); for a linear L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and an n-vector ζ let L_#ζ be the n-vector α ↦ ζ(α∘L), so (LA)_#e = L_#(A_#e). For g : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P differentiable at u, J_g(u) := J_{Dg(u)}. For orthonormal σ₁, …, σₙ, σ_# denotes the n-vector α ↦ α(σ₁, …, σₙ), a unit orientation of span σ. The following algebra (the parent's (L0)–(L2) and the polar/Gram–Schmidt remark of its step 10) is proved here.
(A0) For an n-covector β and an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ: |β(τ)| ≤ |β|_E. Proof: for any orthonormal basis b of ℝ^P, S_b(β) := Σ_{i₁,…,iₙ} β(b_{i₁}, …, b_{iₙ})² does not depend on b (for fixed later arguments, Σ_i γ(b_i, w₂, …)² = |g|² with g the vector representing γ(·, w₂, …) — Parseval — and the slots can be changed one at a time), and S_e(β) = n!|β|²_E (tuples with a repeated index give 0; each injective tuple is a permutation of a unique increasing I and contributes β(e_I)²). Extending τ to an orthonormal basis b and keeping only the n! permutations of τ in S_b(β) gives n!β(τ)² ≤ n!|β|²_E.
(A1) Two unit orientations of the same n-plane differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of the plane then τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O := (⟨τ'_i, τ_j⟩) orthogonal, and multilinear alternating expansion gives α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ) with det O = ±1; so ±τ'_# = ±τ_#. Also −ζ is a unit orientation whenever ζ is.
(A2) Let A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be linear. If A is injective, let σ₁, …, σₙ be the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization of Ae₁, …, Aeₙ, so Ae_j = Σ_{i≤j} T_{ij}σ_i with T upper triangular and T_{jj} = dist(Ae_j, span(Ae₁, …, Ae_{j−1})) > 0. Then (⟨Ae_i, Ae_j⟩) = TᵀT, so J_A = det T = Π_j T_{jj} > 0, and multilinear alternating expansion gives α(Ae₁, …, Aeₙ) = det(T)·α(σ) for every n-covector α, i.e. A_#e = J_A·σ_#, where σ_# is a unit orientation of span σ = A(ℝⁿ). In particular |A_#e(α)| ≤ J_A|α|_E by (A0). Moreover J_A ≤ Π_j|Ae_j| (Hadamard, since T_{jj} ≤ |Ae_j|). If A is not injective, (Ae_j) is linearly dependent, so A_#e = 0 (α alternating) and J_A = 0 (singular Gram matrix); the bounds hold trivially.
(A3) For linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P: J_{LA} ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ·J_A. Proof: if A is not injective, neither is LA and both sides are 0. Otherwise, with σ and T from (A2) and V : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P the isometry Ve_i := σ_i (so A = VT), the Gram matrix of LAe is Tᵀ·(⟨Lσ_i, Lσ_j⟩)·T, hence J_{LA} = det(T)·J_{LV} = J_A·J_{LV}, and J_{LV} ≤ Π_i|Lσ_i| ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ by the Hadamard bound of (A2) applied to LV.
1. Reductions. (a) M₁ := M ∩ K is Borel, Hⁿ(M ∖ M₁) = 0 and Hⁿ(M₁) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M; R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence Q(ω) = ∫_{M₁} θξ(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ for all ω. (b) Oriented points: by (TL) with (U, A, B) := (U, M₁, M) (Hⁿ(M ∩ C) < ∞ for compact C ⊆ U), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ the sets M₁ and M have the same approximate tangent spaces at x; with R.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁, M₁ has an approximate tangent space T_xM₁ at x (unique, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of it. Fix a Borel ξ̃ equal to ξ Hⁿ-a.e. on M (a.e. strong measurability). (c) Cutoff: choose an open V ⊇ K with compact closure ⊆ O and χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, tsupport χ ⊆ V, χ = 1 on an open W₀ ⊇ K; f̂ := χf on O, 0 off O, is C¹ on ℝ^P with compactly supported continuous derivative, hence Lipschitz on ℝ^P (mean value inequality), and f̂ = f on W₀; so f̂(x) = f(x), Df̂(x) = Df(x) for x ∈ K and Q is unchanged when f is replaced by f̂. From now on f denotes f̂; Λ := max(1, sup_K‖Df‖) < ∞.
2. Parametrization (parent step 9; the accepted DAG declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces states the measurable-piece version of (a)–(f), which a decomposition of this node may reuse before applying (g)). There are countably many triples (A_i, G_i, κ_i) with A_i ⊆ ℝⁿ compact, G_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz, differentiable at every u ∈ A_i with DG_i(u) injective, κ_i > 0 and |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| ≥ κ_i|u − v| for u, v ∈ A_i, such that the sets G_i(A_i) ⊆ M₁ are pairwise disjoint and Hⁿ(M₁ ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0. Proof. (a) M₁ ⊆ M is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono): M₁ ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz. (b) Rademacher (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt): D_j := {u : F_j differentiable at u} is Borel with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j) = 0, so Hⁿ(F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j)) = 0 (Lipschitz images of null sets are null; Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). (c) Z_j := {u ∈ D_j : DF_j(u) not injective} satisfies Hⁿ(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 (area formula, the Jacobian vanishing on Z_j; SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero). (d) E_j := (D_j ∖ Z_j) ∩ F_j⁻¹(M₁) is Borel. For injective linear A pick K_A > 0 with |Au| ≥ |u|/K_A and set r(A) := 1/(2K_A); r(A) := 1 otherwise. Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (F_j on E_j with derivative DF_j and this r) gives disjoint Borel t_l covering E_j and A_l = DF_j(y_l), y_l ∈ E_j (so A_l injective), with |F_j(u) − F_j(v) − A_l(u − v)| ≤ r(A_l)|u − v| on E_j ∩ t_l; hence |F_j(u) − F_j(v)| ≥ (2K_{A_l})⁻¹|u − v| there. (e) Enumerate the pieces E_j ∩ t_l as (E_i, G_i, κ_i) (G_i one of the F_j). Disjointify the images: E'_i := E_i ∖ G_i⁻¹(⋃_{i'<i} G_{i'}(E'_{i'})); each G_{i'}(E'_{i'}) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; G_{i'} continuous and injective on E_{i'}), so E'_i is Borel, and the G_i(E'_i) ⊆ M₁ are pairwise disjoint with the same union as the G_i(E_i). (f) M₁ ∖ ⋃_i G_i(E'_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j) ∪ ⋃_j F_j(Z_j) is Hⁿ-null. (g) G_i is injective on E'_i with (1/κ_i)-Lipschitz inverse, so Lⁿ(E'_i) ≤ κ_i^{−n}Hⁿ(M₁) < ∞; by inner regularity E'_i contains disjoint compact sets C_{i,1}, C_{i,2}, … with Lⁿ(E'_i ∖ ⋃_k C_{i,k}) = 0, whose complement's image under G_i is Hⁿ-null. Re-enumerate (C_{i,k}, G_i, κ_i) as (A_i, G_i, κ_i). ∎
3. Lemma T (parent step 10, specialized to globally Lipschitz maps, which covers every use below: the G_i of step 2 and H_i = f∘G_i of step 5). Let A ⊆ ℝⁿ be compact, G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz on ℝⁿ, differentiable at every u ∈ A, and |G(u) − G(v)| ≥ κ|u − v| for u, v ∈ A (κ > 0). Then for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A, V_u := DG(u)(ℝⁿ) is n-dimensional and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G(A)) (G(u)) V_u. Proof. (i) The set of differentiability points of G is Borel and u ↦ DG(u) is Borel on it (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, measurable_fderiv), with ‖DG(u)‖ ≤ Lip(G); so u ↦ 1_A(u)J_G(u) is bounded (by Lip(G)ⁿ, (A2)) and Borel. By the Lebesgue density and differentiation theorems (Mathlib ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub), Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A is a density point of A and a Lebesgue point of 1_A·J_G; fix such u. (ii) DG(u) is injective: for w ≠ 0, density gives points v_r ∈ A with |v_r − (u + rw)| = o(r) as r ↓ 0 (a ball of radius comparable to r about u + rw cannot miss A), and |DG(u)(v_r − u)| ≥ |G(v_r) − G(u)| − o(r) ≥ κ|v_r − u| − o(r), so |DG(u)w| ≥ κ|w|. Hence J_G(u) > 0 and dim V_u = n. (iii) Put x := G(u) and let h ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with tsupport h ⊆ B_ρ(0). By the scaling Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(S) and the injective area formula for the Lipschitz map G on A, on which it is injective (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, or injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn / weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum; their Jacobian within A equals J_G at a.e. point of A), ∫_{η_{x,r}(G(A))} h dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A h((G(v) − x)/r)J_G(v) dv = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_A(u + rw)·h((G(u + rw) − G(u))/r)·J_G(u + rw) dw. The integrand vanishes unless |w| < ρ/κ (if u + rw ∈ A then |G(u + rw) − G(u)| ≥ κr|w|). On B_{ρ/κ}(0), (G(u + rw) − G(u))/r → DG(u)w uniformly as r ↓ 0 (differentiability at u), h is uniformly continuous and bounded, and ∫_{B_{ρ/κ}}|1_A(u + rw)J_G(u + rw) − J_G(u)| dw → 0 (u is a Lebesgue point of 1_A·J_G with value J_G(u)). So the integral tends to J_G(u)∫_{ℝⁿ} h(DG(u)w) dw = ∫_{V_u} h dHⁿ (area formula for the injective linear map DG(u)). As h is arbitrary, G(A) has approximate tangent space V_u at G(u). ∎
4. Tangent planes of M₁ and the orientation (★). Fix i. G_i(A_i) ⊆ M₁ is compact. By (TL) with (A, B) := (G_i(A_i), M₁), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ G_i(A_i) the approximate tangent spaces of G_i(A_i) and M₁ at x agree. Since (G_i|A_i)⁻¹ is (1/κ_i)-Lipschitz, Hⁿ-null subsets of G_i(A_i) have Lⁿ-null preimages in A_i, and G_i maps Lⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets. With Lemma T and step 1(b): for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A_i, x := G_i(u) is oriented, ξ̃(x) = ξ(x), and T_xM₁ = DG_i(u)(ℝⁿ). By (A2) with A := DG_i(u) (injective), DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u) is a unit orientation of DG_i(u)(ℝⁿ) = T_xM₁, as is ξ(x); so by (A1), for such u,
 (★) ξ(G_i(u)) = s_i(u)·DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u), s_i(u) ∈ {1, −1},
 where s_i(u) := 1 if ξ̃(G_i(u)) = DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u) and −1 otherwise (Borel in u).
5. The maps H_i := f∘G_i (parent step 11). H_i is Lipschitz on ℝⁿ, differentiable at each u ∈ A_i with DH_i(u) = Df(G_i(u))∘DG_i(u) (chain rule), and DH_i(u)_#e = Df(G_i(u))_#(DG_i(u)_#e). By (★), for a.e. u ∈ A_i and every n-covector β: ξ(G_i(u))(β∘Df(G_i(u))) = s_i(u)·⟨β, DH_i(u)_#e⟩/J_{G_i}(u). By (A3), J_{H_i}(u) = J_{Df(G_i(u))DG_i(u)} ≤ ‖Df(G_i(u))‖ⁿJ_{G_i}(u) ≤ ΛⁿJ_{G_i}(u), and by (A2), |⟨β, DH_i(u)_#e⟩| ≤ J_{H_i}(u)|β|_E for every n-covector β (⟨β, ζ⟩ := ζ(β)).
6. Pulling Q back. The injective area formula for G_i on A_i (Hⁿ⌞G_i(A_i) is the image of J_{G_i}·Lⁿ⌞A_i under G_i) and step 2 give, with θ_i := θ∘G_i, for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): Q(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i(u)s_i(u)⟨ω(H_i(u)), DH_i(u)_#e⟩ du, and Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_iJ_{H_i} du ≤ ΛⁿΣ_i∫_{A_i} θ_iJ_{G_i} du = Λⁿ∫_{M₁} θ dHⁿ < ∞, so the series converges absolutely (by step 5, the u-integrand is bounded by sup|ω|_E·θ_iJ_{H_i}).
7. Bi-Lipschitz pieces of H_i. Where DH_i(u) is not injective, DH_i(u)_#e = 0 (A2) and the integrand of step 6 vanishes. A_i⁺ := {u ∈ A_i : DH_i(u) injective} is Borel (u ↦ DH_i(u) is Borel on A_i; injectivity means det(⟨DH_i(u)e_p, DH_i(u)e_q⟩) ≠ 0). As in step 2(d), (g) (partition lemma with r(A) := 1/(2K_A), then inner regularity), A_i⁺ is, up to an Lⁿ-null set, a countable disjoint union of compact sets A_{il} with |H_i(u) − H_i(v)| ≥ κ_{il}|u − v| on A_{il}, κ_{il} > 0.
8. Image pieces. N_{il} := H_i(A_{il}) is compact and H_i|A_{il} is injective with (1/κ_{il})-Lipschitz inverse. Put g_{il} := (θ_is_i)∘(H_i|A_{il})⁻¹ on N_{il} (values in ℤ ∖ {0}) and η_{il} := (DH_i(·)_#e/J_{H_i}(·))∘(H_i|A_{il})⁻¹ (unit orientations of DH_i(u)(ℝⁿ) by (A2), Borel on N_{il}). The injective area formula for H_i on A_{il} turns step 6 into Q(ω) = Σ_{i,l} ∫_{N_{il}} g_{il}(y)⟨ω(y), η_{il}(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y), with Σ_{i,l}∫_{N_{il}} |g_{il}| dHⁿ = Σ_{i,l}∫_{A_{il}} θ_iJ_{H_i} du ≤ Λⁿ∫_{M₁}θ dHⁿ < ∞. N := ⋃_{i,l} N_{il} is Borel (σ-compact), N ⊆ f(M₁) ⊆ f(K) ⊆ U, and Hⁿ(N) ≤ Σ_{i,l}∫_{N_{il}}|g_{il}| < ∞ (|g_{il}| ≥ 1).
9. Common tangent planes. By Lemma T (H_i on A_{il}) and (TL) with (U, A, B) := (ℝ^P, N_{il}, N) (Borel, Hⁿ(N) < ∞), with the null-set transfer through the bi-Lipschitz map H_i|A_{il} as in step 4: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N and every (i, l) with y ∈ N_{il}, N has approximate tangent space T_yN = DH_i(u)(ℝⁿ), u := (H_i|A_{il})⁻¹(y) (countably many null exceptional sets). Hence η_{il}(y) is a unit orientation of T_yN, and by (A1) η_{il}(y) = ε_{il}(y)η(y) with ε_{il}(y) ∈ {±1}, where η(y) := η_{i₀l₀}(y) for the first piece (in a fixed enumeration) containing y; η is Borel. As Σ_{i,l}|g_{il}|1_{N_{il}} is integrable, Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N lies in only finitely many N_{il}.
10. Integer multiplicity. For such y, Σ_{i,l} g_{il}(y)1_{N_{il}}(y)η_{il}(y) = k(y)η(y) with k(y) := Σ_{(i,l): y∈N_{il}} ε_{il}(y)g_{il}(y) ∈ ℤ (a finite sum) and |k| ≤ Σ_{i,l}|g_{il}|1_{N_{il}}. By dominated convergence (the partial sums are dominated by Σ|g_{il}|1_{N_{il}}·sup|ω|_E), Q(ω) = ∫_N k(y)⟨ω(y), η(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
11. The representation (positive multiplicity). Choose a Borel Hⁿ-null N₀ ⊆ N off which steps 9–10 hold and k agrees with a Borel ℤ-valued k̃. Put N' := {y ∈ N ∖ N₀ : k̃(y) ≠ 0}, θ' := |k̃| (ℕ-valued, Borel) and ξ' := sign(k̃)·η. Then (N', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U: N' is Borel and N' ⊆ N ⊆ U; N' is countably n-rectifiable (N ⊆ ⋃_i H_i(ℝⁿ) with H_i Lipschitz on ℝⁿ); θ' is measurable with θ' ≥ 1 on N'; ∫_{N'∩C} θ' dHⁿ ≤ Σ_{i,l}∫|g_{il}| < ∞ for every compact C; ξ' is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable; and by (TL) with (A, B) := (N', N), for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N' the approximate tangent space of N' at y equals T_yN, which ξ'(y) = ±η(y) orients (IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign). Finally, for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ∫_{N'} θ'ξ'(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{N'} k⟨ω, η⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_N k⟨ω, η⟩ dHⁿ = Q(ω), since k = 0 on N ∖ (N' ∪ N₀). So Q = τ(N', θ', ξ') and Q is integer multiplicity. ∎
